hook.line: Altamira offers to buy the café and Tomás wants to say no in a way nobody can misread. Spanish has a firm no, a cheeky no, and a careful no for when you might be wrong.
hook.es: De ninguna manera vendo el café.
hook.en: There's no way I'm selling the café.

examples.en: There's no way I'm going to apologise.

examples.es: No hay razón alguna para cancelar.
examples.en: There is no reason whatsoever to cancel.

examples.es: No ha llamado nadie, que yo sepa.
examples.en: Nobody has called, as far as I know.

examples.es: No tenemos problema alguno, que yo sepa.
examples.en: We have no problem at all, as far as I know.

rule:
Four ways to say no with extra weight.

*De ninguna manera*: no way. Firm, neutral, works with anyone. Also *de ningún modo*.
*¡Que no, te digo!*: no, I'm telling you. Casual, a bit impatient, with friends.
*No hay razón alguna*: no reason whatsoever. Formal. Put *alguno* after the noun, and keep *no* before the verb.
*No…, que yo sepa*: not as far as I know. A soft no that leaves room for being wrong.

No extra *no* is needed after *de ninguna manera*, but the other forms do keep it.
smallPrint: Teachers call *que yo sepa* a restrictive clause: it limits your claim to what you know. The *sepa* is a subjunctive.

readAndPick.es: No ha llamado nadie, que yo sepa.
options: Nobody has called, as far as I know.

readAndPick.es: No hay razón alguna para esperar.
options: There is some reason to wait.
There is no reason whatsoever to wait.
I don't have a reason to leave.

readAndPick.es: Que yo sepa, no hay problema.
options: As far as I know, there's no problem.
We have no problem at all.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (There's no way I'm selling the café): De ninguna ___ vendo el café. (manera / razón)
yourTurn.answer: De ninguna manera vendo el café.
accept: De ningún modo vendo el café.
yourTurn.why: The firm no is *de ninguna manera*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (There is no reason whatsoever to cancel): No hay razón ___ para cancelar. (alguna / ninguna)
yourTurn.answer: No hay razón alguna para cancelar.
accept: No hay ninguna razón para cancelar.
yourTurn.why: *Alguna* goes after the noun and the *no* stays before the verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (to a friend, impatient): No, I'm telling you!
Type in Spanish: Nobody has called, as far as I know.
yourTurn.answer: No ha llamado nadie, que yo sepa.
accept: Que yo sepa, no ha llamado nadie.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it softer by adding as far as you know: No hay problema.
yourTurn.answer: No hay problema, que yo sepa.
accept: Que yo sepa, no hay problema.
yourTurn.why: You add *que yo sepa* at the end.
*De ninguna manera* starts the sentence and no second *no* is needed.

pitfalls.wrong: De ninguna manera no pienso disculparme.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *De ninguna manera* already carries the negative, so skip the extra *no*.

pitfalls.right: No hay razón alguna para cancelar.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Alguna* in this meaning needs *no* before the verb.

pitfalls.wrong: No ha llamado nadie, que yo sé.
pitfalls.right: No ha llamado nadie, que yo sepa.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The fixed phrase uses *sepa*, not *sé*.

personal: Say one thing you would never do, starting with *de ninguna manera*.
